title: Review round 1: web client attachment UI
notes:
SEC2: No efficiency issues for MVP single-file scenario. O(n²) filter (line 593), sequential upload (line 564), and renderAttachmentPreview calls all operate on minimal data sets appropriate for MVP (1 file per send). Recommend revisit if multi-file attachment is added later.
Calibration (SEC7): Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. The attachment feature is ~200 lines of new code. Security surface (XSS via textContent, download URL encoding) was explicitly checked and appears solid. Correctness risks were covered by SEC0 (found the real bug: silent attachment loss on send failure). Field names, URL template handling, filename preservation were validated. Integration points (Message/set, uploadBlob round-trip, optimistic UI + real replacement) were examined; no logic gaps found. Running out of real complaints: yes. Remaining two findings are purely stylistic (missing JSDoc, consistency of innerHTML vs textContent for clearing) with no engineering basis.
SEC1 Maintainability Review Complete — 3 P1 bugs found:

1. KITH-d5g1.4: sendMessage fails to restore pendingAttachments on send failure — user loses selected files
2. KITH-d5g1.5: Race condition — Send button clickable while file uploads pending — wrong attachments sent to next message
3. KITH-d5g1.6: uploadBlob assumes session.uploadUrl exists, crashes if missing (no defensive guard)

Plus 2 P2 issues:
- uploadBlob returns generic error for all 4xx/5xx (no distinction for user guidance)
- File input handler overwrites error messages when multiple uploads fail

All other aspects assessed: LOW RISK.
- pendingAttachments state initialization and mutation are clear
- renderAttachmentPreview() coupling is explicit and sequential
- FileList handling correctly uses Array.from()
- Bootstrap timing is correct (session ready before setupCompose)
